**Finding: Compliant (no redline required).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — subsections (a)–(g) impose substantive use limits only (no copying, no reverse engineering, no service bureau use); there is no compliance-audit, self-reporting or access mechanism attached to them.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — limited to time-of-the-essence and notice provisions.
- **§ 14 (Confidentiality)** — mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within the definition of Confidential Information; it creates no inspection right.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** — a bare payment obligation with no true-up or usage-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises* and *monitor* surfaced nothing operative.

Since no audit right binds us — and in particular no right of access to our systems — the AUDIT rule's risks (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise. Inserting the preferred frequency/notice/cost parameters would require first creating an audit right that Garman does not currently have, which would be worse for us than silence. Accordingly, no edit is proposed.
